project.description_en: At the end of the theme, the child shows how to sit and stand well, signs “please”, “thank you” and “sorry”, names a sour, a sweet and a bitter food and explains why alcohol, cigarettes and blades are not for children.

activities.goal_en: Recite a mathematical rhyme about the body.
activities.prompt_en: Say the rhyme and show your fingers and toes.
steps_en: Say the rhyme once with gestures.
Say it line by line.
Say it together.
Count fingers and toes at the end.
observe_en: Shows the right number of fingers.
Counts to 20 with fingers and toes.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 34 (Poetry and Rhymes: Rhymes), p. 61; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.story_en:
Ten little fingers to hold my spoon,
Ten little toes to dance to the tune,
Ten and ten, let us count them, friends:
Twenty little helpers at my ends!

activities.goal_en: Use simple signs for polite words and welcome people with special needs.
activities.prompt_en: Some friends cannot hear. We can speak with our hands too. This is “please”.
steps_en: Show “please”: a flat hand moving in a circle on the chest.
Show “sorry”: a fist moving in a circle on the chest.
Show “thank you”: fingertips from the chin moving forward.
Practise in pairs without speaking.
observe_en: Uses a sign at the right moment.
Shows respect for friends who are different.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 35 (Sign Language and Gestures: Manners), p. 62; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: One-armed robot letters: r, i, n
activities.goal_en: Write letters that go down and back up: r, i, n.
activities.prompt_en: Like a robot arm: go down, come back up and go over. Let us write r, i and n.
steps_en: Show the movement in the air: down, back up, over.
Trace r, i and n in sand.
Trace them on dotted lines.
Write a row of each letter.
observe_en: Goes down then back up without lifting.
Keeps the letters on the line.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 37 (Writing: Pre-letter formation), p. 64; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: A French song for washing hands
activities.goal_en: Sing a short French song for pleasure.
activities.prompt_en: Sing with me in French while we wash our hands: “Je lave, je lave mes mains, avec du savon, c’est bien !”
steps_en: Sing the line slowly.
The child repeats while miming the hand washing.
Sing it while really washing hands.
Ask: what is “savon” in English? (soap)
observe_en: Gives the meaning of one French word.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 38 (French: Chants), p. 65; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Fingers and toes: adding up to 20
activities.goal_en: Add two numbers up to 20 with fingers, toes or objects.
activities.prompt_en: You have 10 fingers. Add 5 toes. How many in all?
steps_en: Show 10 fingers.
Add 5 toes, counting on: eleven, twelve…
Say the total.
Try other sums with sticks.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 39 (Mathematics: Mathematical operations), p. 66–67; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

interactive.prompt_en: 10 fingers and 5 toes. How many in all?
interactive.explanation_en: Start at 10 and count on five: eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen. There are 15.

activities.goal_en: Tell a gentle touch from a rough touch and choose to touch gently.
activities.prompt_en: A good friend touches gently. A rough touch can hurt. Show me a gentle touch on your arm.
steps_en: Touch a doll gently, then show (without hurting) what rough means.
Ask: which one feels good?
Practise gentle touches: a high five, a soft tap on the shoulder.
Say: if someone touches you roughly or in a way you do not like, say “Stop!” and tell an adult.
observe_en: Knows to say “Stop!” and tell an adult.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 41 (Sensory and Perceptive Education: The sense of touch), p. 71–72; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Distinguish sweet, bitter and sour tastes.
activities.prompt_en: Taste a little: is it sweet like a pawpaw, bitter like bitter leaf or sour like a lime?
steps_en: Prepare small pieces: pawpaw, a drop of lime juice, cooked bitter leaf.
Taste one at a time and make the face.
Name the taste.
Sort pictures of food by taste.
observe_en: Tastes only what the adult gives.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 41 (Sensory and Perceptive Education: The sense of taste), p. 71–72; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Not for children: alcohol, cigarettes, blades
activities.goal_en: Stay away from alcohol, cigarettes and dangerous sharp objects.
activities.prompt_en: Alcohol and cigarettes make the body sick. Razor blades and broken glass cut. We do not touch them; we call an adult.
steps_en: Show pictures: a bottle of beer, a cigarette, a razor blade, broken glass.
Say why each one is dangerous for children.
Act: a child finds a blade and calls an adult.
Make a “Not for me!” poster.
observe_en: Says they will not touch them.
Calls an adult in the role play.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 48 (Health Education and Nutrition: Good health habits), p. 81; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Practise neatness: clean nails, tidy clothes, a clean face.
activities.prompt_en: A neat child has clean hands and nails, a clean face and tidy clothes.
steps_en: Look at the hands and nails together.
Wash the face and hands.
Tuck in the shirt and button it well.
Look in a mirror and smile.
observe_en: Notices when something is not neat.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 45 (Character Education: Simple etiquette), p. 78; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Protect oneself from burns by hot water and hot oil at home.
activities.prompt_en: Hot water and hot oil burn the skin. We stay away from the stove and we never pull a pot handle.
steps_en: Show a picture of a kitchen with a pot on the fire.
Point to hot things.
Act: the child stays one big step away from the stove.
Say what to do after a small burn: cool water and call an adult.
observe_en: Names hot water and oil as dangers.
Says “cool water and call an adult”.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 47 (Safety Education: Home safety), p. 80; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Paint by stamping with the hands and fingers.
activities.prompt_en: Put your hand in the paint and press it on the paper. Now make little dots with your finger!
steps_en: Prepare washable paint in plates.
Press the whole hand on paper.
Add finger prints to make a pattern or a picture.
Describe the picture to a friend.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 51 (Painting: Practice), p. 84; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery Two contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery Two teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Build balance by walking on hands and feet and stretching.
activities.prompt_en: Walk like a bear on your hands and feet! Now stretch up tall like a tree.
steps_en: Warm up: stretch arms and legs.
Walk on hands and feet across a mat or grass.
Walk backwards slowly.
Finish by stretching and breathing calmly.
observe_en: Moves with hands and feet in coordination.
source_refs: Nursery Two, table 53 (Physical Education and Sports: Gymnastics), p. 86; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

scale.description: Succeeds mostly with a model or help.
Sometimes succeeds alone, sometimes with a reminder.
Succeeds on their own in a familiar situation.

indicators: Adds fingers and toes up to 20.
Tells a gentle touch from a rough touch.
Names sweet, bitter and sour foods.
Keeps away from alcohol, cigarettes and blades.

sources: Cameroon Nursery School Curriculum, English Subsystem, MINEDUB, 2018: table 13 (integrated learning themes), p. 37; Nursery Two tables, cited and not reproduced.
